clue.text: Home Office branch last to refurbish fully

parts.note: being at home is being in, so home gives IN
a department, abbreviated DEPT, is a branch of an office or ministry

indicators.note: last to points at the final letter of the word refurbish

explanation.surface: The Home Office has a department that is the last to get a complete makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to refurbish' supplies H, the final letter of 'refurbish'.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something in depth is to study it thoroughly, so the phrase is an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Distinct details about superpower

parts.note: info, short for information, means details
C stands for circa, Latin for about
the US is the world's leading superpower

explanation.surface: The particulars concerning a superpower are clear and separate.
explanation.definitionFit: An image in focus is sharp and clear rather than blurred, so it is distinct.

clue.text: British artist sculpted duke with alarming hat

indicators.note: sculpted means shaped anew, so the letters are remodelled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A British artist carved a nobleman wearing a frightening piece of headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpted' signals the anagram of DUKE plus ALARMING HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura Knight was an English painter made a Dame, famed for circus and ballet scenes.

clue.text: Wealthy leader's funny dog caught traitor

parts.note: Pluto is the cartoon dog of Disney fame
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: A rich man's comic pet dog caught a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'leader's' stands for 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is one who rules or holds power because of great riches.

clue.text: Concert venue first to exclude northern orchestra

parts.note: a venue for concerts

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the word exclude

explanation.surface: A concert hall is the first to shut out an orchestra from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to exclude' gives E. The Hallé is Manchester's symphony orchestra, in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hallé is a long-established symphony orchestra based in Manchester, a northern English city.

clue.text: Tenor tackling new work gets support in studio

indicators.note: tackling is read as taking on, so one word grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: the tenor of something is its general drift or mood
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A tenor learning a fresh piece is given some backing in the recording studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' is not the singer but the sense of overall tone, MOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A monopod is a single-legged stand that steadies a camera, a piece of photographic studio support.

clue.text: Aberrant, erratic emphasis placed on noun

indicators.note: erratic means wandering unpredictably, so the letters of the word stray into a new order

parts.note: N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: An unusual, unpredictable stress lands on a noun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' signals the anagram of EMPHASIS, and 'placed on' sets N after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misshapen deviates from its normal form, as aberrant things depart from the norm.

clue.text: Updated drainage system, reversing initial direction

indicators.note: the first letter is a compass point, and reversing it swaps south for north

parts.note: a sewer is a drain carrying waste water

explanation.surface: A modernised drains network that changes its opening flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing initial direction' turns the leading S (south) of SEWER into N (north).
explanation.definitionFit: Something updated is more recent than before, so it is newer.

clue.text: Science feature on ancient medicine filling empty pages

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so the pieces sit within the outer letters
empty means hollowed out, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: a feature is a newspaper article
physic is an old word for medicine

explanation.surface: A magazine feature about old remedies occupies the blank pages of a science journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty pages' leaves PS, which ARTICLE and PHYSIC fill.
explanation.definitionFit: Particle physics is the branch of science studying subatomic particles and their forces.

clue.text: Seemingly removes autograph from drawings

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the word looks like taking off one's signature

explanation.surface: Someone appears to take the signature off some pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is playful: split DE-SIGNS as if un-signing.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs are plans or sketches showing how something will look, so drawings.

clue.text: Et tu Brute? How wrong I was!

definitions.meaning: Julius Caesar's dying words in Shakespeare, literally the famous final words of a famous man
the phrase is used ironically of a confident statement soon proved spectacularly wrong

explanation.surface: Caesar's reproach to his friend, followed by a rueful admission of misjudgement.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a celebrity's dying utterance and, ironically, an overconfident claim that events then refute.

clue.text: Instrument could indicate hail, given another tap

indicators.note: taps are marked H for hot and C for cold, so switching to the other tap swaps one of those letters for the other

parts.note: to hail someone is to greet them, to say hello

explanation.surface: A puzzling hint about how a musical instrument might signal hailstones with an extra knock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given another tap' plays on the H and C marked on bathroom taps: the hot H of HELLO becomes the cold C.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Bidding hard to relieve pressure in shipping abroad

indicators.note: to relieve someone is to take over their post, so one letter stands in for another

parts.note: exporting is sending goods abroad by ship or otherwise
P is the physics symbol for pressure
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone bids hard to ease the pressure on overseas shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to relieve' has H (hard) take the place of P (pressure) in EXPORTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Bidding someone do something is urging or exhorting them, so the two participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Old fogey rejected dessert and paid

parts.note: a square is an old-fashioned, conventional person

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for dessert is read backwards

parts.note: PUD is British slang for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A stuffy old man turned down his pudding and settled the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns PUD into DUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to settle a debt or bill, so it means having paid what is owed.

clue.text: Lengths first spanned by balls

indicators.note: spanned by means bridged across, so one word stretches around the other

parts.note: balls are formal dances
first is written 1ST, read as the letters IST

explanation.surface: A sporting note about distances first covered by balls in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls' suggests sports equipment, but here they are formal social occasions; first is read as 1ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Distances are measured extents, lengths between points.

clue.text: Piece of metal used for part of joint

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of metal is employed to make part of a joint, as in metalwork or surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'for', but that is a link word joining wordplay to definition; 'part of joint' alone can stand in for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The talus is the ankle bone, which forms part of the ankle joint with the leg bones.

clue.text: Depart suspiciously with Nutmeg's media player

indicators.note: suspiciously suggests something fishy, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: Nutmeg is the setter, so the setter's 'has' is I've

explanation.surface: The setter leaves furtively, carrying a media player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspiciously' scrambles DEPART to TAPEDR; 'Nutmeg's' is the setter saying 'I've'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape drive is a device that reads and plays data or recordings stored on magnetic tape.

clue.text: Base time indicated

parts.note: base in the sense of low or ignoble is mean

explanation.surface: A terse note that a basic time was shown, as on a clock or timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: If something meant a thing, it signified or pointed to it, so both are past tenses of signifying.

clue.text: Maudlin knight hampered by desire to follow mum

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, so this piece goes after the word for mum

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: hampered by means hemmed in by, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: a wish is a desire
K is the chess abbreviation for king, and also used for knight in honours

explanation.surface: A sentimental knight is held back by his longing to imitate his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly sentimental, much as maudlin means tearfully sentimental.

clue.text: Bird seed with smoother coating

indicators.note: coating means covering, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a sander is a tool that smooths wood
a pip is a seed, as in an apple

explanation.surface: Birdseed given a smooth outer layer, like a coated feed pellet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoother' is not a comparative adjective but a tool that smooths.
explanation.definitionFit: The sandpiper is a wading shorebird of the family that includes curlews and snipe.

clue.text: Brooded quietly at home, cutting grass

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so these letters go inside the word for grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
at home means in

explanation.surface: Someone sulked silently at home while mowing the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or be discontented, so having brooded over something.

clue.text: Was single potty adequate receptacle for drinker?

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters of the words are jumbled madly

explanation.surface: Mock question whether a lone chamber pot would do as a vessel for a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' looks like a chamber pot, but it signals the anagram of WAS SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wineglass is a stemmed glass from which a drinker takes wine, a fit vessel for the purpose.

clue.text: Ball game void without pitch

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the emptied word goes round the other
void means emptied, so only the word's outside letters remain

parts.note: to lob is to pitch or throw high

explanation.surface: A ball game rendered null because there is no playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; 'pitch' is a throw, not a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A globe is a sphere, the same shape as a ball.

clue.text: Diocesan council, say, ignoring a show of consent

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: taken as written
a nod is a gesture of agreement

explanation.surface: A church council where, for example, nobody bothers with a formal sign of agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring a' takes A out of SAY, leaving SY.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church members governing a diocese or church.

clue.text: Lines adopted by party harden

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so the party's letters go round the lines

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party
RY abbreviates railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A political party takes on a party line and stiffens its stance.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: When something dries up, it loses moisture and stiffens, so the phrasal verb can mean set hard.

clue.text: Little-used ruling leading to beneficial qualification

indicators.note: leading to means coming before, so the pieces run in clue order

parts.note: a party that is ruling is in power, so in
something beneficial is good
a condition is a qualification or proviso attached to a statement

explanation.surface: An obscure legal ruling results in a profitable proviso.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little-used' sounds like an obscure ruling, but it defines an item with little wear, as in a used-car advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-hand item with little wear is described in sales listings as being in good condition.

clue.text: Husband picked up reference book lacking top cover

indicators.note: picked up means caught by ear, so the word for reference book is given as it is pronounced

parts.note: an atlas is a reference book of maps

explanation.surface: A husband grabbed a reference work, evidently without a lid on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' says ATLAS is heard, spelt ATLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat is the cover worn on top of the head, so someone hatless lacks one.

clue.text: Got into line, prepared for a roasting

definitions.meaning: soldiers dress their ranks when they align themselves in a straight row
a bird is ... when it is cleaned and trussed ready for the oven

explanation.surface: Someone lined up obediently, braced for a severe telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing is both the military act of aligning ranks and the kitchen task of readying poultry.
